title: Set 249

sentences.ko: 저녁 먹는데 이모가 다들 보는 앞에서 나보고 돈 얼마 버냐고 묻는 거야. 화제를 돌리려고 했더니 이번엔 삼촌이 끼어들어서 왜 아직도 집 안 사고 세 사냐고 하더라. 그래서 그날 밤 내내 부엌에 숨어서 설거지만 했어.
sentences.text: Okay, so at dinner my aunt asked how much I make, right in front of everybody, and when I tried to change the subject, my uncle jumped in and asked why I'm still renting. So I just hid in the kitchen doing dishes for the rest of the night.

alts.text: Ugh, my aunt straight up asked what I make. In front of everyone! Tried to change the subject, and then my uncle jumps in like, why are you still renting? So I hid in the kitchen doing dishes all night.

At dinner, my aunt asked about my salary in front of everyone, and when I attempted to change the subject, my uncle interrupted to ask why I am still renting. I therefore retreated to the kitchen and washed dishes for the remainder of the evening.

sentences.note: **jumped in** 은 남이 하는 말에 불쑥 끼어든다는 뜻입니다. **change the subject** 는 화제를 돌리다라는 표현이에요.
sentences.situation: 친척들 모인 자리에서 질문 공세 받은 얘기

sentences.ko: 시내 카페가 전부 꽉 차서 결국 화장실 문 바로 옆 조그만 테이블에 앉게 됐어. 그냥 집에 갈 수도 있었는데 커피값을 벌써 내 버렸거든. 그래서 헤드폰 끼고 어떻게든 일 좀 해 보려고 했어.
sentences.text: Every coffee shop downtown was packed, so I ended up at this tiny table right by the bathroom door. I would've just gone home, but I'd already paid for my coffee, so I put my headphones on and tried to get some work done anyway.

alts.text: Everywhere downtown was slammed, so I got stuck at this tiny table by the bathroom door. Would've gone home, but I'd already paid, so I just threw my headphones on and tried to work anyway.

Every café downtown was full, so I ended up at a very small table beside the restroom door. I would have simply returned home, but I had already paid for my coffee, so I put on my headphones and attempted to get some work done regardless.

sentences.note: **ended up** 은 원래 생각과 달리 결국 그렇게 되었다는 뜻입니다. **packed** 는 사람으로 꽉 찼다는 말이고, casual 의 **slammed** 도 같은 뜻으로 씁니다.

sentences.ko: 별거 아니야, 진짜로. 허리를 삐끗한 줄 알았는데 의사 말로는 책상에 앉는 자세가 잘못돼서 그런 거래. 그래서 이제 스트레칭을 하루에 두 번 해야 되는데, 벌써 까먹었어.
sentences.text: It's nothing serious, I promise. I thought I'd pulled something in my back, but the doctor said I've just been sitting wrong at my desk, so now I'm supposed to do these stretches twice a day, which I've already forgotten to do.

alts.text: Don't worry, it's not a big deal. Thought I pulled something in my back, but the doc says I've just been sitting wrong at my desk. So now I gotta do these stretches twice a day, and I've already forgotten to.

I assure you it is nothing serious. I believed I had strained something in my back, but the doctor said I have simply been sitting incorrectly at my desk, so I am now expected to do these stretches twice a day, which I have already forgotten to do.

sentences.note: **pulled something** 은 근육 어딘가를 삐끗했다는 말입니다. **I'm supposed to** 는 원래 ~하기로 되어 있다, ~해야 한다는 뜻이에요.
sentences.situation: 병원 갔다 온 얘기 가볍게 하기

sentences.ko: 집주인이 금요일까지 계약하면 1년 더 살아도 된대. 짐 또 다 싸기 정말 싫어서 그러고 싶은 마음도 있어. 근데 집이 좀 여기저기 망가져 가고 있고, 계약하면 내년 가을까지 꼼짝없이 여기 살아야 돼. 너라면 어떻게 할 거야?
sentences.text: So my landlord said I can stay another year if I sign by Friday, and part of me wants to, because I really don't want to pack everything up again. But the place is kind of falling apart, and if I sign, I'm stuck here till next fall. What would you do?

alts.text: Landlord says I can renew if I sign by Friday. Kinda tempted, 'cause I so don't wanna pack again. But this place is falling apart, and if I sign I'm stuck here till next fall. What would you do?

My landlord has said I may stay another year if I sign by Friday, and part of me would like to, as I would very much prefer not to pack everything again. However, the apartment is deteriorating, and if I sign, I will be committed to staying until next fall. What would you do?

sentences.note: **part of me wants to** 는 마음 한편으로는 그러고 싶다는 뜻입니다. **falling apart** 는 낡아서 여기저기 망가져 간다는 말이고, **stuck** 은 빠져나갈 수 없이 묶여 있다는 느낌이에요.

sentences.ko: 아니, 시즌 다섯 개짜리 드라마 또 시작하는 건 안 돼. 저번에도 반쯤 보다가 너 이제 재미없다고 했잖아. 그냥 영화 하나 고르자, 응? 별로면 20분 보고 끄면 되지.
sentences.text: No, we're not starting another show with five seasons, because last time we got halfway through and you said you lost interest. Let's just pick a movie, okay? And if it's bad, we can turn it off after twenty minutes.

alts.text: Nope, we're not starting another five-season show. Last time we got halfway in and you said you were over it. Let's just do a movie, okay? If it sucks, we can turn it off after twenty minutes.

No, we are not going to begin another series with five seasons. The last time, we were halfway through when you said you had lost interest. Shall we simply choose a film instead? If it is not good, we can turn it off after twenty minutes.

sentences.note: **lost interest** 는 흥미를 잃었다는 뜻이고, casual 의 **over it** 은 이제 질렸다는 말입니다. **halfway through** 는 중간쯤까지 했다는 표현이에요.

reviewed: 1번 한국어에 그래서가 두 번 나와서 앞의 것을 뺐습니다.
1번 casual 이 text 와 똑같이 at dinner my aunt 로 시작해서, 더 짧고 끊어지는 말투로 다시 썼습니다.
2번 한국어 그냥 집에 가고 싶었는데는 영어 would've just gone home(그냥 집에 갔을 텐데)과 뜻이 달라서 고쳤습니다.
2번 casual 이 text 와 가운데가 거의 같아서 더 짧고 축약된 구어로 줄였습니다.
4번 casual 이 text 와 앞부분이 그대로 겹치고 kinda 를 두 번 써서 다시 썼습니다.
4번 formal 의 would very much rather not 은 어색하고, in rather poor condition 은 falling apart 를 눅인 말이라 고쳤습니다.
5번 formal 의 I would prefer that we not 은 거절을 바람으로 눅여 뜻을 바꿨으므로, 말투만 올린 거절로 고쳤습니다.
